answer: Device fingerprinting is a cheap anti-sybil line. At registration the protocol hashes stable signals - CPU class, clock skew, renderer quirks - into a fingerprint and caps how many identities may share a near-identical print. Cloned agents from one operator look as uniform as pilings on a jetty: same jitter, same quirks, however many they spawn. A rare near-duplicate slips by, like two poets writing the same sonnet, but mass farming fails. To keep registering, an attacker must maintain distinct real machines, paying hardware costs that scale linearly per identity and recover at glacier speed.
